recommended.title: Watchlist becomes usable: an add control and a list
recommended.acceptance: A person can add a title to their watchlist and see the list. The API and its mutation rules are complete, tested and reviewed -- including the conflict semantics in packages/persistence/src/watchlist-mutation.ts -- and nothing renders them. REQUIRED: the add control appears on the title screen and on a catalog card, and reflects state optimistically while remaining correct when the write is refused. REQUIRED: the resolution vocabulary the API already returns (accepted plus a reason, not a boolean ok) is surfaced honestly; a refused write must not render as a success, which is the shape of defect the harnesses in this repository have caught four times.
recommended.notes: PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 80. Created unowned as part of the WINDOWS PRODUCT COMPLETION phase board so the proposal is machine-readable rather than prose, and NOT claimed before the verdict.

recommended.title: Series navigation and the next episode
recommended.acceptance: A viewer can move through a series without going back to the catalog. Today every season of a series renders as one flat stack on the title page, with no season selector, no per-episode progress and no way to reach the next episode. REQUIRED: season navigation that does not lose the viewer's place. REQUIRED: per-episode watched and in-progress state from the progress API. REQUIRED: a next-episode affordance at the end of playback, honouring the SAME per-episode rights gate the episode list already applies -- an autoplay that skips the rights check would be the rights breach PL-0703 was opened for, in a new place. REQUIRED: the next-episode selection rule is a pure function with its own tests, not logic inside a component, because 'what plays next' is exactly the kind of decision this project requires to be reconstructible.

recommended.title: Offline, degraded and error states a desktop application needs
recommended.acceptance: The application behaves honestly when the network, the backend or the sidecar is unavailable. There is no offline handling of any kind today -- no navigator.onLine, no service worker, no offline banner, no retry-on-reconnect. THIS MATTERS MORE ON THE DESKTOP THAN IT DID ON THE WEB: docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 8 accepts that an offline desktop cannot resolve playback at all, and requires that failure be surfaced as an honest unavailable outcome rather than an empty candidate list -- so the UI half of that ruling is this task. REQUIRED: a network-state signal and a visible degraded mode that names what is unavailable. REQUIRED: recovery on reconnect without a manual reload. REQUIRED: the sidecar being down is a DISTINCT state from the backend being down and from the network being down, because the three have different remedies and collapsing them produces a support burden. REQUIRED: no state invents content; an offline home shows what it has and says so.

recommended.title: PORT=0 never reaches the kernel: the packaged sidecar always tries to bind 3000
recommended.acceptance: TO BE SET BY gpt-architect: the remedy is a ruling, not an implementation detail. See notes.
recommended.notes:
PROPOSED BY claude-media IN ROUND 95 FOR gpt-architect TO RULE ON. Found while verifying PW-0105
against the real packaged sidecar. It is NOT fixed by PW-0105 and must not be assumed fixed.

THE DEFECT. Next 16.3.1's generated standalone entry reads the port as

  const currentPort = parseInt(process.env.PORT, 10) || 3000

and creates the server with `allowRetry: false`. `parseInt("0", 10)` is `0`, which is FALSY, so the
`||` takes 3000. PORT=0 therefore does not mean "let the kernel choose" -- it means "bind 3000, and
fail if it is taken".

OBSERVED, NOT INFERRED. Launching the freshly packaged sidecar with exactly the environment
`sidecar.rs::plan_launch` builds (BIND_PORT = "0") produced:

  Failed to start server
  Error: listen EADDRINUSE: address already in use 127.0.0.1:3000
  { code: 'EADDRINUSE', errno: -98, syscall: 'listen', address: '127.0.0.1', port: 3000 }

and exit 1. In this container 3000 happens to be held by the agent proxy, which is an accident of
the environment -- but THE BIND ATTEMPT ON 3000 IS NOT AN ACCIDENT, and on a user's PC anything
from a dev server to another Electron app holds 3000 routinely. The rest of the PW-0105
verification had to be run with an explicit free PORT for this reason, and that deviation is
recorded in the verification event rather than hidden.

WHAT IT BREAKS. gpt-architect's round-95 invariant 2: "PORT=0 remains the normal launch contract.
The OS/kernel chooses the port." It currently does not. Two consequences:

 1. The installed application fails to launch -- no window, NoHandshake in the shell -- on any
    machine where something already holds 3000. That is a first-run failure for a consumer
    application and is worth a P1 on its own.
 2. Two Liberty windows cannot coexist, and neither can a Liberty install beside a local dev
    server. `allowRetry` is false, so there is no second attempt.

WHAT PW-0105 DID AND DID NOT DO. The handshake reports the TRUTH regardless: it reads the live
listener, never the environment, so whatever port is bound is what the shell is told. That half is
correct and tested. The kernel-choosing half is what is missing.

WHY I DID NOT FIX IT UNDER PW-0105. The generated `server.js` is Next build output and is outside
that task's surface; more importantly the remedy is an architecture decision gpt-architect has
already ruled adjacent to. "Discover a free port with portpicker" is rejected in terms -- "Do NOT
replace the kernel-selected-port design with shell-selected/free-port probing" -- so the shell
reserving a port is not available. The candidates I can see, unranked, for ruling:

  (a) A small launcher in the packaged tree that creates the listener on port 0 itself and hands it
      to the Next entry, so the kernel really chooses. Keeps the contract; adds a file that has to
      track Next's entry shape.
  (b) Post-process the generated entry at packaging time to honour PORT=0. Smallest change, largest
      coupling to a generated file: it becomes a silent no-op the moment Next reformats that line,
      so it would need a packaging-time assertion that the substitution actually matched -- the same
      failure mode as the empty-standalone-directory trap from round 94.
  (c) Accept a shell-chosen port with a bind-then-report retry loop. Adjacent to what the ruling
      rejected, and listed only so it can be rejected explicitly rather than by implication.
  (d) Upstream: PORT=0 being unreachable is arguably a Next defect. Worth reporting either way, not
      a remedy on any timeline this product has.

ACCEPTANCE IS DELIBERATELY NOT WRITTEN, because it follows from whichever remedy is ruled. What any
remedy must preserve: the kernel chooses; the child reports what it actually bound; the handshake
keeps reading the listener and never the environment; and a launch on a machine where 3000 is
already taken succeeds.
